article_title: Oakland International High School: A Thriving Community School for Oakland's Newcomer Students
citation: Charlie Thompson. (2023). Oakland International High School: A Thriving Community School for Oakland's Newcomer Students. Learning Policy Institute. https://learningpolicyinstitute.org
title: Wellness Center and Coordination of Services Team coordinating partnerships and supports
description: The Wellness Center, funded by the district and the Oakland Fund for Children and Youth, provides "a centralized infrastructure, dedicated staff, and a structured process for services and referrals." It houses two case managers, a dean of culture and community, an academic counselor who is also a clinical therapist, and college and career resources. Its staff meet weekly as the Coordination of Services Team (COST) to identify students newly in need of support and update on previously identified students; since spring 2021 students can refer themselves via QR code, and the community school manager reports that "direct services are getting to students quicker."
requirements: A community school manager to coordinate partnerships, funding, and resources
District and philanthropic funding for the center and its staff
target_learners: Newcomer high school students and their families
target_learning_goals: Removing out-of-school barriers to attendance and academic success
examples: Most medical referrals go through the TechniClinic, a district school-based health center partnership with La Clinica de la Raza serving two nearby campuses
key_sources: Charlie Thompson. (2023). Oakland International High School: A Thriving Community School for Oakland's Newcomer Students. Learning Policy Institute. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=ED642542

article_title: Oakland International High School: A Thriving Community School for Oakland's Newcomer Students
citation: Charlie Thompson. (2023). Oakland International High School: A Thriving Community School for Oakland's Newcomer Students. Learning Policy Institute. https://learningpolicyinstitute.org
title: Learning Lab: educator pipeline and dissemination initiative for newcomer education
description: Opened in 2017 in partnership with the Reach Institute, the Learning Lab builds educator capacity for newcomer education through "school site visits, professional development workshops, and research projects." It also prepared pre- and in-service educators via two credential pathways: working as a teacher of record with mentoring and coaching, or spending a year as a Learning Lab assistant in a mentor teacher's classroom. In its first year it supported 12 teacher candidates and 1 administrative candidate; 2 years later, 18 teacher candidates and 11 administrator candidates, growth the report says helped the school largely solve its own vacancy problem.
requirements: Private funding for credential pathways (scaled back beginning in 2022–23, after which staff directed aspiring teachers to state- and district-funded residency programs)
constraints: Private funding for the pathways was scaled back beginning in the 2022–23 school year
target_learners: Pre- and in-service educators serving newcomer students
examples: Five Newcomer Learning Lab assistants have become teachers or case managers at Oakland International, and two others teach in newcomer pathways elsewhere in the district
key_sources: Charlie Thompson. (2023). Oakland International High School: A Thriving Community School for Oakland's Newcomer Students. Learning Policy Institute. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=ED642542

article_title: ChatGPT-generated help produces learning gains equivalent to human tutor-authored help on mathematics skills
citation: Pardos ZA, Bhandari S (2024) ChatGPT-generated help produces learning gains equivalent to human tutor-authored help on mathematics skills. PLoS ONE 19(5): e0304013. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0304013
title: OATutor: open-source adaptive tutoring platform with CC-licensed human-authored hints used to deliver the study
description: OATutor (Open Adaptive Tutor) is the open-source tutoring system the authors used as "the base platform to deliver the OpenStax derived questions with hints authored by human tutors from the OATutor Project". It logs condition, objective name, anonymized user ID, problem name, correctness, hint request actions, and timestamps, and its human-authored hints were produced by screened UC Berkeley undergraduates with editor quality checks. The study content is released under a Creative Commons license and the system source code on GitHub for full replication.
requirements: Questions and hints must be text-only, since the study excluded problems depending on images or figures
target_learners: Mechanical Turk adult learners with at least a high school degree
secondary and early post-secondary mathematics students
target_learning_goals: probability and statistics (independent and mutually exclusive events)
examples: The study delivered three-question pre-tests, five-question acquisition phases with hints, and repeated three-question post-tests through OATutor across four OpenStax subjects
key_sources: Pardos ZA, Bhandari S (2024) ChatGPT-generated help produces learning gains equivalent to human tutor-authored help on mathematics skills. PLoS ONE 19(5): e0304013. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0304013

article_title: The impact of AI anxiety on career decisions of college students
citation: Duan, N., Li, L., Lin, G. & Chen, H. (2026). The impact of AI anxiety on career decisions of college students. Scientific Reports. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-37648-y
title: OASIS-based AI Anxiety Scale (5-item, Chinese-adapted)
description: The article adapted the Overall Anxiety Severity and Impairment Scale (OASIS) and a brief Chinese anxiety scale into a 5-item, unidimensional AI Anxiety Scale measuring "the frequency of anxiety episodes, severity, avoidance behaviours, and functional impairment in work/academic and social domains", with references to anxiety concretised as AI-triggered (e.g., feeling anxious due to AI). It showed α = 0.939 in this study and correlated moderately (r = 0.68) with Wang and Wang's AIAS on a subsample (n = 89), suggesting convergent but not redundant validity.
requirements: Independent construct validation, since the article states it measures anxiety symptoms triggered by AI rather than AI-specific cognitive appraisals
constraints: The authors interpret results as 'AI-triggered anxiety' rather than a distinct AI anxiety construct pending full validation
target_learning_goals: assessment of AI-triggered anxiety in career development research
examples: Used in a questionnaire survey of 315 Chinese college students with five-point Likert response format and translation-back-translation procedure
key_sources: Duan, N., Li, L., Lin, G. & Chen, H. (2026). The impact of AI anxiety on career decisions of college students. Scientific Reports. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-37648-y

article_title: The Impact of Online Algorithm Visualization on ICT Students' Achievements in Introduction to Programming Course
citation: Fatih Saltan. (2017). The Impact of Online Algorithm Visualization on ICT Students' Achievements in Introduction to Programming Course. Journal of Education and Learning, 6(1). https://doi.org/10.5539/jel.v6n1p184
title: OAV design characteristics: scaffolding with videos and clues, explorative activities, and ordered visual commands
description: Students identified design features of the OAV environment that supported their learning: scaffolding elements "including videos and clues", which they called "very helpful and instructive"; learning through discovery that made them more active; and activities in which they "learned to put visual commands in the right place and in the right order, otherwise the applications would not work", which they said improved their progressive thinking skills. One student described code.org as "a good practice environment that enables users to learn coding following a unique strategy that involves tips and videos".
requirements: Scaffolding elements such as videos and clues embedded in the activities
target_learners: novice programmers beginning an introduction to programming course
examples: Treatment students completed code.org activities in which misplaced or misordered visual commands caused the application not to work, prompting them to reason about order and placement.
key_sources: Fatih Saltan. (2017). The Impact of Online Algorithm Visualization on ICT Students' Achievements in Introduction to Programming Course. Journal of Education and Learning, 6(1). https://doi.org/10.5539/jel.v6n1p184
grain_size: lesson-to-unit sequence of visual programming activities

article_title: Design and practice of blended teaching of internal medicine nursing based on O-AMAS effective teaching model.
citation: Duan Anyan, Jiang Fen, Li Ling, Li Qun, Chen Wei. (2024). Design and practice of blended teaching of internal medicine nursing based on O-AMAS effective teaching model. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-024-05588-8
title: O-AMAS effective teaching model
description: O-AMAS is a five-link, online-offline hybrid interactive teaching model developed by Nankai University's effective teaching team in 2017, comprising Objective, Activation, Multi-learning, Assessment, and Summary. The article states it "is oriented by learning results and driven by benign interaction" and "advocates student-centered" teaching that inspires students to become knowledge builders and problem solvers. In this study it structures the design of a blended internal medicine nursing course, from SMART- and Bloom-aligned objectives through activation, diversified methods, assessment with feedback, and student-led summary.
requirements: A teaching team spanning department head, pedagogy experts, subject teachers, and a platform teaching assistant to design, implement, and integrate online and offline components
constraints: The article notes limitations in the number of courses applied, class hours, and sample size
Prior applications cited are in pharmacology, microbial physiology, and community pharmacist training
target_learners: higher education students in health sciences
examples: The TIA section staged pre-class self-directed learning at knowledge/comprehension levels, in-class cooperative learning at application/analysis/synthesis, and post-class consolidation at evaluation level
key_sources: Duan Anyan, Jiang Fen, Li Ling, Li Qun, Chen Wei. (2024). Design and practice of blended teaching of internal medicine nursing based on O-AMAS effective teaching model. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-024-05588-8

article_title: Design and practice of blended teaching of internal medicine nursing based on O-AMAS effective teaching model.
citation: Duan Anyan, Jiang Fen, Li Ling, Li Qun, Chen Wei. (2024). Design and practice of blended teaching of internal medicine nursing based on O-AMAS effective teaching model. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-024-05588-8
title: O-AMAS blended course design with five linked stages
description: The course design pattern arranges a blended course in five parts matching the O-AMAS links: multi-dimensional objectives (macro knowledge/ability/quality goals plus per-lesson micro objectives across Bloom's six bands), activation of students physically, emotionally, and cognitively, diversified teaching methods (LBL, TBL, PBL, CBL), process-plus-final assessment with feedback, and a brief student-led summary using platform-generated hot words or mind maps. The article summarizes the design in Fig. 1 and applies it across pre-class, in-class, and post-class stages.
requirements: Online platforms (MOOC, Chaoxing) integrated with offline classroom and clinical internship
Assessment aligned to both low-order and high-order objectives
constraints: Designed and evaluated for a single core clinical nursing course; the article notes limitations in number of courses, class hours, and sample size
target_learning_goals: internal medicine nursing theory and practice
examples: Acute leukemia teaching used a micro-video prompting the discussion topic "Does the blood of patients with leukemia turn white?" followed by brainstorming on the Chaoxing platform
key_sources: Duan Anyan, Jiang Fen, Li Ling, Li Qun, Chen Wei. (2024). Design and practice of blended teaching of internal medicine nursing based on O-AMAS effective teaching model. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-024-05588-8

article_title: Design and practice of blended teaching of internal medicine nursing based on O-AMAS effective teaching model.
citation: Duan Anyan, Jiang Fen, Li Ling, Li Qun, Chen Wei. (2024). Design and practice of blended teaching of internal medicine nursing based on O-AMAS effective teaching model. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-024-05588-8
title: Internal medicine nursing assessment system combining process and final assessment
description: The course team developed a comprehensive assessment and evaluation system combining process evaluation and final evaluation from online and offline sources. Table 1 prints the weights: question-answer process in class 5%, chapter quiz 5%, topic discussion 10%, group activities 10%, clinical noviceship 10%, and final exam 60%, with forms spanning offline, online, and online + offline. Assessment content covers both low-order goals (knowledge, comprehension) and high-order goals (application, analysis, synthesis, evaluation), and feedback is used to adjust teaching strategies.
requirements: Alignment of assessment methods with teaching objectives
Online platform support for engagement tracking and dynamic feedback
constraints: Weights are specific to this internal medicine nursing course
target_learning_goals: achievement of knowledge and higher-order nursing objectives
examples: Group discussion based on clinical progressive cases, topic discussion, and thinking questions were used as multiple assessment forms for practical evaluation and feedback

article_title: A Simple, Reproducible and Low-cost Simulator for Teaching Surgical Techniques to Repair Obstetric Anal Sphincter Injuries.
citation: Knobel Roxana, Volpato Lia Karina, Gervasi Liliam Cristini, Viergutz Raquel de Almeida, Trapani Alberto Júnior. (2018). A Simple, Reproducible and Low-cost Simulator for Teaching Surgical Techniques to Repair Obstetric Anal Sphincter Injuries. RBGO Gynecology & Obstetrics. https://doi.org/10.1055/s-0038-1668527
title: Low-cost handmade OASIS repair simulator built from condom, chocolate bar, cotton cloth, and beef strips
description: A fourth-degree tear model assembled from everyday materials: "A condom with a chocolate bar inserted in it represented the rectal mucosa and the intestinal contents", a cotton cloth flap represented the internal anal sphincter, and a beef strip with longitudinally running fibers represented the external anal sphincter. It cost approximately R$10.00, was assembled with the aid of anatomical photos, and supported practicing end-to-end and overlapping repair techniques with real surgical instruments and suture material.
requirements: Surgical material (tweezers, needle holder, scissors, Allis clamp) and suture; anatomical photos to determine the structures and function of each component
constraints: The article states it was not possible to accurately reproduce the anatomy, which other models such as goat or pig anal sphincter do more effectively
target_learning_goals: diagnosis and surgical repair of obstetric anal sphincter injuries
anatomy and physiology of the anal sphincter complex
examples: Simulations lasted approximately 2 hours each in classrooms of two public hospitals, with about 12 participants per session during 2017
key_sources: Knobel Roxana, Volpato Lia Karina, Gervasi Liliam Cristini, Viergutz Raquel de Almeida, Trapani Alberto Júnior. (2018). A Simple, Reproducible and Low-cost Simulator for Teaching Surgical Techniques to Repair Obstetric Anal Sphincter Injuries. RBGO Gynecology & Obstetrics. https://doi.org/10.1055/s-0038-1668527
